export const RealmSettingsTabs = () => {
  const { adminClient } = useAdminClient();
  const { t } = useTranslation();
  const { addAlert, addError } = useAlerts();
  const { realm: realmName, realmRepresentation: realm, refresh } = useRealm();
  const combinedLocales = useLocale();
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  const isFeatureEnabled = useIsFeatureEnabled();
  const [tableData, setTableData] = useState<
    Record<string, string>[] | undefined
  >(undefined);
  const form = useForm({
    mode: "onChange",
  });
  const { control, setValue, getValues } = form;
  const [key, setKey] = useState(0);
  const refreshHeader = () => {
    setKey(key + 1);
  };

  const setupForm = (r: RealmRepresentation = realm!) => {
    convertToFormValues(r, setValue);
  };

## The trace

### 1. Admin UI (React) — where a realm is read

`RealmContextProvider` is the single place the console loads the current realm. It calls the TS admin client through the `useFetch` helper and holds the result in `RealmContext`, which every screen gets via `useRealm()`:

- `js/apps/admin-ui/src/context/realm-context/RealmContext.tsx:47` — `useFetch(() => adminClient.realms.findOne({ realm }), setRealmRepresentation, [realm, key])`
- The `adminClient` instance itself is built in `js/apps/admin-ui/src/admin-client.tsx` (`initAdminClient`), which sets `baseUrl = environment.adminBaseUrl` and registers a token provider backed by `keycloak-js`.

### 2. TypeScript admin client — resource → agent → fetch

- `js/libs/keycloak-admin-client/src/resources/realms.ts` — the `Realms` resource, `path: "/admin/realms"`. `findOne` = `GET /{realm}` (with `catchNotFound`), `update` = `PUT /{realm}`.
- `Resource.makeRequest` / `Resource.makeUpdateRequest` (`resource.ts`) just forward to the `Agent`.
- `Agent.request` / `Agent.updateRequest` split payload into URL params / query params / body, then `Agent.#requestWithParams` expands the URL template, attaches `Authorization: Bearer …` and calls `fetchWithError`.

So `findOne` → `GET {adminBaseUrl}/admin/realms/{realm}`, `update` → `PUT {adminBaseUrl}/admin/realms/{realm}`.

### 3. Admin UI — where a realm is written (two distinct paths)

**(a) the plain admin API**, used by most tabs/dialogs — e.g. `LoginTab`'s `updateSwitchValue` calls `adminClient.realms.update({ realm }, …)`. (Same shape in `EventsTab`, `OtpPolicy`, `PasswordPolicy`, `WebauthnPolicy`, `CibaPolicy`, `BindFlowDialog`, `RevocationModal`.)

**(b) the Realm Settings form**, which deliberately bypasses the typed client: `RealmSettingsTabs.save` does a raw `fetchWithError(… , "PUT")` to `admin/realms/{realm}/ui-ext`, sending a `UIRealmRepresentation` (a `RealmRepresentation` plus `upConfig`). The matching read-only helper for console-specific realm info is `fetchRealmInfo`/`fetchAdminUI` → `GET …/ui-ext/info`.

### 4. Java server side — JAX-RS routing

- `AdminRoot` is `@Path("/admin")`; `AdminRoot.getRealmsAdmin` is `@Path("realms")` and authenticates the bearer token.
- `RealmsAdminResource.getRealmAdmin` is `@Path("{realm}")`: resolves the `RealmModel` by **name**, sets it on the session context, builds the `AdminPermissionEvaluator` and `AdminEventBuilder`, and returns `RealmAdminResource`.
- `RealmAdminResource.getRealm` (`@GET`) — `auth.realm().canViewRealm()` then `ModelToRepresentation.toRepresentation(session, realm, false)`; otherwise it falls back to a trimmed representation under `requireViewRealmNameList()`.
- `RealmAdminResource.updateRealm` (`@PUT`) — `requireManageRealm()`, blocks renaming `master`, runs `ReservedCharValidator` / SMTP / keypair / certificate validation, then `RepresentationToModel.updateRealm(...)`, fires `StoreSyncEvent`, emits the `UPDATE` admin event, returns 204.

### 5. Java server side — the `ui-ext` extension hop

- `RealmAdminResource.extension` is `@Path("{extension}")`: it looks up an `AdminRealmResourceProvider` by the path segment, so `/ui-ext` resolves to `AdminExtProvider` (`getId() == "ui-ext"`, gated on `Feature.ADMIN_V2`) → `AdminExtResource`.
- `AdminExtResource.realm()` is `@Path("/")` → `UIRealmResource`.
- `UIRealmResource.updateRealm` **delegates to `RealmAdminResource.updateRealm`** and, only if that succeeded, applies the user-profile part via `UserProfileResource.setAndGetConfiguration(rep.getUpConfig())`. `UIRealmResource.getInfo` serves `GET /ui-ext/info`.
- `org.keycloak.admin.ui.rest.model.UIRealmRepresentation` is the Java counterpart of the TS `UIRealmRepresentation` (realm rep + `upConfig`).

### 6. Model layer

- Read: `ModelToRepresentation.toRepresentation(KeycloakSession, RealmModel, boolean, boolean)` maps `RealmModel` → `RealmRepresentation`.
- Write: `RepresentationToModel.updateRealm` is a thin hop to `session.getProvider(DatastoreProvider.class).getExportImportManager().updateRealm(...)`, i.e. `DefaultExportImportManager.updateRealm`, which does the rename plus the field-by-field application onto `RealmModel`. The SPI contract is `ExportImportManager.updateRealm`.

Notes on confidence: everything above is read directly from source. The only entry I'd flag as *one representative of many* is `LoginTab.tsx#updateSwitchValue` — it is a genuine caller of `realms.update`, but there are ~8 equivalent call sites; I listed it rather than all of them so the plain-PUT path has a concrete UI origin. `UIRealmsResource#getRealms` (the `ui-ext/realms/names` list used by the realm selector) is adjacent but is realm *listing*, not single-realm read/update, so I left it out.

result:
## The trace

### 1. Admin UI (React) — where a realm is read

`RealmContextProvider` is the single place the console loads the current realm. It calls the TS admin client through the `useFetch` helper and holds the result in `RealmContext`, which every screen gets via `useRealm()`:

- `js/apps/admin-ui/src/context/realm-context/RealmContext.tsx:47` — `useFetch(() => adminClient.realms.findOne({ realm }), setRealmRepresentation, [realm, key])`
- The `adminClient` instance itself is built in `js/apps/admin-ui/src/admin-client.tsx` (`initAdminClient`), which sets `baseUrl = environment.adminBaseUrl` and registers a token provider backed by `keycloak-js`.

### 2. TypeScript admin client — resource → agent → fetch

- `js/libs/keycloak-admin-client/src/resources/realms.ts` — the `Realms` resource, `path: "/admin/realms"`. `findOne` = `GET /{realm}` (with `catchNotFound`), `update` = `PUT /{realm}`.
- `Resource.makeRequest` / `Resource.makeUpdateRequest` (`resource.ts`) just forward to the `Agent`.
- `Agent.request` / `Agent.updateRequest` split payload into URL params / query params / body, then `Agent.#requestWithParams` expands the URL template, attaches `Authorization: Bearer …` and calls `fetchWithError`.

So `findOne` → `GET {adminBaseUrl}/admin/realms/{realm}`, `update` → `PUT {adminBaseUrl}/admin/realms/{realm}`.

### 3. Admin UI — where a realm is written (two distinct paths)

**(a) the plain admin API**, used by most tabs/dialogs — e.g. `LoginTab`'s `updateSwitchValue` calls `adminClient.realms.update({ realm }, …)`. (Same shape in `EventsTab`, `OtpPolicy`, `PasswordPolicy`, `WebauthnPolicy`, `CibaPolicy`, `BindFlowDialog`, `RevocationModal`.)

**(b) the Realm Settings form**, which deliberately bypasses the typed client: `RealmSettingsTabs.save` does a raw `fetchWithError(… , "PUT")` to `admin/realms/{realm}/ui-ext`, sending a `UIRealmRepresentation` (a `RealmRepresentation` plus `upConfig`). The matching read-only helper for console-specific realm info is `fetchRealmInfo`/`fetchAdminUI` → `GET …/ui-ext/info`.

### 4. Java server side — JAX-RS routing

- `AdminRoot` is `@Path("/admin")`; `AdminRoot.getRealmsAdmin` is `@Path("realms")` and authenticates the bearer token.
- `RealmsAdminResource.getRealmAdmin` is `@Path("{realm}")`: resolves the `RealmModel` by **name**, sets it on the session context, builds the `AdminPermissionEvaluator` and `AdminEventBuilder`, and returns `RealmAdminResource`.
- `RealmAdminResource.getRealm` (`@GET`) — `auth.realm().canViewRealm()` then `ModelToRepresentation.toRepresentation(session, realm, false)`; otherwise it falls back to a trimmed representation under `requireViewRealmNameList()`.
- `RealmAdminResource.updateRealm` (`@PUT`) — `requireManageRealm()`, blocks renaming `master`, runs `ReservedCharValidator` / SMTP / keypair / certificate validation, then `RepresentationToModel.updateRealm(...)`, fires `StoreSyncEvent`, emits the `UPDATE` admin event, returns 204.

### 5. Java server side — the `ui-ext` extension hop

- `RealmAdminResource.extension` is `@Path("{extension}")`: it looks up an `AdminRealmResourceProvider` by the path segment, so `/ui-ext` resolves to `AdminExtProvider` (`getId() == "ui-ext"`, gated on `Feature.ADMIN_V2`) → `AdminExtResource`.
- `AdminExtResource.realm()` is `@Path("/")` → `UIRealmResource`.
- `UIRealmResource.updateRealm` **delegates to `RealmAdminResource.updateRealm`** and, only if that succeeded, applies the user-profile part via `UserProfileResource.setAndGetConfiguration(rep.getUpConfig())`. `UIRealmResource.getInfo` serves `GET /ui-ext/info`.
- `org.keycloak.admin.ui.rest.model.UIRealmRepresentation` is the Java counterpart of the TS `UIRealmRepresentation` (realm rep + `upConfig`).

### 6. Model layer

- Read: `ModelToRepresentation.toRepresentation(KeycloakSession, RealmModel, boolean, boolean)` maps `RealmModel` → `RealmRepresentation`.
- Write: `RepresentationToModel.updateRealm` is a thin hop to `session.getProvider(DatastoreProvider.class).getExportImportManager().updateRealm(...)`, i.e. `DefaultExportImportManager.updateRealm`, which does the rename plus the field-by-field application onto `RealmModel`. The SPI contract is `ExportImportManager.updateRealm`.

Notes on confidence: everything above is read directly from source. The only entry I'd flag as *one representative of many* is `LoginTab.tsx#updateSwitchValue` — it is a genuine caller of `realms.update`, but there are ~8 equivalent call sites; I listed it rather than all of them so the plain-PUT path has a concrete UI origin. `UIRealmsResource#getRealms` (the `ui-ext/realms/names` list used by the realm selector) is adjacent but is realm *listing*, not single-realm read/update, so I left it out.
